subject: math.CT
name: Pivotal structure conjecture for fusion categories
statement: Does every fusion category over C admit a pivotal structure, that is, a monoidal natural isomorphism from the identity functor to the double-dual functor?
importance: Would give a uniform duality and trace formalism for all finite semisimple tensor categories.
status_note: Known for pseudo-unitary categories and many other classes; arbitrary fusion categories are not assumed to be pseudo-unitary.

references.title: Etingof, Nikshych and Ostrik, On fusion categories

subject: math.CT
name: Rank finiteness for fusion categories
statement: For every positive integer r, are there only finitely many equivalence classes of fusion categories over C with exactly r isomorphism classes of simple objects?
importance: Would reduce classification at each rank to a finite problem.
status_note: Rank finiteness is proved for modular categories. The entry asks about all fusion categories, a broader class.

references.title: Bruillard, Ng, Rowell and Wang, Rank-finiteness for modular categories

subject: math.CT
name: Categorical Frobenius divisibility conjecture
statement: For a fusion category C over C and a simple object X, must FPdim(C)/FPdim(X) be an algebraic integer?
importance: Extends Frobenius divisibility of group representation degrees to arbitrary fusion categories.
status_note: Known for weakly group-theoretical categories and several other families; the unrestricted fusion-category statement is open.

references.title: Etingof, Nikshych and Ostrik, Weakly group-theoretical and solvable fusion categories

subject: math.CT
name: Weakly integral fusion categories conjecture
statement: Is every fusion category over C with integer Frobenius–Perron dimension weakly group-theoretical, meaning Morita equivalent to a category obtained by successive finite-group extensions from Vec?
importance: Would give a structural classification of a large class of tensor categories using finite groups.
status_note: The weakly group-theoretical class includes all known weakly integral examples; this does not claim that all such categories are group-theoretical.

references.title: Etingof, Nikshych and Ostrik, Weakly group-theoretical and solvable fusion categories

subject: math.CT
name: Property F conjecture for braided fusion categories
statement: If a braided fusion category C over C is weakly integral, must every braid-group representation on Hom(Y,X^{⊗n}), obtained from its braiding, have finite image for all objects X,Y and n≥1?
importance: Links arithmetic properties of tensor categories to finiteness of quantum braid representations.
status_note: Known for weakly group-theoretical braided categories and many explicit families. The question includes weakly integral categories beyond those cases.

references.title: Naidu and Rowell, A finiteness property for braided fusion categories
Li and Ruan, Generalized property F for weakly group-theoretical modular fusion categories

subject: math.CT
name: Vertex-operator-algebra realization of unitary modular categories
statement: Is every unitary modular tensor category braided equivalent to the representation category of a unitary rational C_2-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type?
importance: Would realize all algebraic anyon models as chiral conformal field theories.
status_note: Many lattice, affine, and other examples are realized; arbitrary unitary modular categories are still outside a general realization theorem.

references.title: Wang and Wang, In and around Abelian anyon models

subject: math.CT
name: Conformal-net realization of unitary modular categories
statement: Is every unitary modular tensor category braided equivalent to the category of finite-index representations of some completely rational local conformal net?
importance: Connects tensor-category classification with analytic constructions of quantum field theory.
status_note: Established for several important families; the general conformal-net realization problem remains open.

references.title: Bischoff, Conformal Net Realizability of Tambara–Yamagami Categories and Generalized Metaplectic Modular Categories
Wang and Wang, In and around Abelian anyon models

subject: math.CT
name: Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for coherator groupoids
statement: For a Grothendieck coherator, does the associated category of weak infinity-groupoids, localized at its homotopy-group equivalences, present the homotopy theory of spaces?
importance: Would validate Grothendieck’s algebraic globular description of arbitrary homotopy types.
status_note: The homotopy hypothesis is proved for many other models of weak groupoids. This entry specifically concerns Grothendieck coherator groupoids.

references.title: Algebraic coherators, controlled theories, and Grothendieck realizations

subject: math.CT
name: General weak-unit semistrictification conjecture
statement: Can all homotopy types be modeled by non-unital strict infinity-categories in which every horizontal, vertical, and whiskering composition is defined and compatible, with weak units and weak inverses, as in Henry’s general version of Simpson’s conjecture?
importance: Asks how much coherence can be made strict without losing the homotopy information of spaces.
status_note: Henry’s regular version is proved, and later regular semistrict models are known. The more restrictive general version with all strict composition operations is the question here.

references.title: Henry, Regular polygraphs and the Simpson conjecture

subject: math.CT
name: Freyd generating hypothesis
statement: In the stable homotopy category, must a map between finite spectra be zero if it induces zero on all stable homotopy groups?
importance: Asks whether a basic homological functor faithfully detects morphisms in a central triangulated category.
status_note: This is the original finite-spectra hypothesis; some analogues in derived or representation categories are false or have different answers.
